topics.titleUr: ڈیٹا سٹرکچر (Data Structure) پروگرام میں ڈیٹا کو ترتیب دینے کا طریقہ ہ…
topics.speakEn: 3.1 Data Structures in Python. A data structure is a way of organising values in a program so you can store them, find them and change them. Every useful program is built on data structures. Python gives you two layers: Primitive data structures — the basic types that hold one value. Examples: integers ( int ), floating-point numbers ( float ), and booleans ( bool ). Abstract data structures — higher-level containers built from primitive types so you can hold many values and run richer operations. Examples: lists, tuples, sets, dictionaries . Python has these four abstract structures built in. You do not install anything extra. That is why collecting marks, names or settings is simpler in Python than in many other languages. One value versus a collection. A student’s age is one integer. That student’s three test marks need a list. age = 17 height = 5.8 passed = True marks = [80, 75, 90] print(type(age)) print(type(height)) print(type(passed)) print(type(marks)) <class 'int'> <class 'float'> <class 'bool'> <class 'list'> type() tells you which structure a value has. age is a primitive
topics.speakUr: ڈیٹا سٹرکچر (Data Structure) پروگرام میں ڈیٹا کو ترتیب دینے کا طریقہ ہے۔ پرائمیٹو اقسام جیسے عدد (int) صرف ایک قیمت رکھتی ہیں، جبکہ فہرست، ٹیپل، سیٹ اور ڈکشنری کئی قیمتیں ایک ساتھ سنبھالتی ہیں۔ پائتھن میں یہ چاروں سٹرکچرز پہلے سے موجود ہیں، اس لیے ڈیٹا جمع کرنا دوسری زبانوں کے مقابلے میں آسان ہے۔

topics.titleUr: فہرست (List) مربع بریکٹ [] میں لکھی جاتی ہے، ترتیب برقرار رکھتی ہے اور…
topics.speakEn: 3.1.1 Lists (Ordered, Mutable, Methods). A list is Python’s most versatile built-in data structure. It stores an ordered collection of items in a single variable. Lists are mutable (you can change them after you create them) and they are written with square brackets [] . Why use a list? One variable can hold thousands of values. You can mix types if you need to. You can add, remove and sort items as the program runs. Worked example: methods change the same list step by step. fruits = ['apple', 'banana', 'apple'] print(fruits) fruits.append('grape') print(fruits) fruits.remove('apple') print(fruits) fruits.sort() print(fruits) ['apple', 'banana', 'apple'] ['apple', 'banana', 'apple', 'grape'] ['banana', 'apple', 'grape'] ['apple', 'banana', 'grape'] After this line List in memory create ['apple', 'banana', 'apple'] .append('grape') ['apple', 'banana', 'apple', 'grape'] .remove('apple') ['banana', 'apple', 'grape'] — only the first apple goes .sort() ['apple', 'banana', 'grape'] More methods on numbers: nums = [10, 20, 30] print(len(nums)) nums.insert(1, 15) print(nums) print(nums.coun
topics.speakUr: فہرست (List) مربع بریکٹ [] میں لکھی جاتی ہے، ترتیب برقرار رکھتی ہے اور تبدیل کی جا سکتی ہے (Mutable)۔ انڈیکس صفر سے شروع ہوتا ہے، اور [-1] آخری عنصر دیتا ہے۔ .append() آخر میں جوڑتا ہے، .remove() پہلی مشابہ قیمت ہٹاتا ہے، اور .sort() اصل فہرست کو ترتیب دیتا ہے۔ تلاش کرتے وقت break مل جانے کے بعد لوپ روک دیتا ہے۔

topics.titleUr: ٹیپل (Tuple) گول بریکٹ () میں لکھا جاتا ہے، ترتیب رکھتا ہے مگر تبدیل ن…
topics.speakEn: 3.1.2 Tuples (Ordered, Immutable). A tuple is an ordered collection that is immutable — once created, you cannot add, remove or replace items. Think of it as a read-only list . Tuples use parentheses () . Like lists, they allow duplicates, mixed types, and indexing from 0 (including negative indices). When to choose a tuple. A student’s roll number, name and class form a record that should not be edited in place: record = ("XII-CS-07", "Ayesha", "Computer Science") print(record[0]) print(len(record)) XII-CS-07 3 If later you need to change the class, you build a new tuple. You do not assign to record[2] .
topics.speakUr: ٹیپل (Tuple) گول بریکٹ () میں لکھا جاتا ہے، ترتیب رکھتا ہے مگر تبدیل نہیں ہو سکتا (Immutable)۔ انڈیکس اور سلائس فہرست جیسی ہیں، لیکن t[0] = 99 سے TypeError آتا ہے۔ صرف دو میتھڈز ہیں: .count() اور .index() ۔ حساس ڈیٹا کے لیے ٹیپل محفوظ ہے۔ اگر ٹیپل کے اندر فہرست ہو تو اس فہرست کے اندر کی اشیاء بدل سکتی ہیں۔

topics.titleUr: سیٹ (Set) منفرد عناصر کا بغیر ترتیب اور بغیر انڈیکس مجموعہ ہے، جو {} م…
topics.speakEn: 3.1.3 Sets (Unordered, Unique, Math Operations). A set stores an unordered, unindexed collection of unique elements. It is inspired by mathematical sets. You write a set with curly braces {} . Duplicates are removed as soon as the set is created. Because there is no index, myset[0] is illegal. The set itself is mutable (you can add and remove items). Each item inside must be immutable (numbers, strings, tuples of immutables — not lists). Deduplication. A teacher types roll numbers and some are repeated. A set keeps each roll once: rolls = [12, 5, 12, 8, 5, 19] unique = set(rolls) print(unique) print(sorted(unique)) {8, 19, 12, 5} [5, 8, 12, 19] set(rolls) drops duplicates. sorted(unique) gives a list in numeric order for a register.
topics.speakUr: سیٹ (Set) منفرد عناصر کا بغیر ترتیب اور بغیر انڈیکس مجموعہ ہے، جو {} میں لکھا جاتا ہے۔ دہرائی ہوئی قیمتیں خود بخود ختم ہو جاتی ہیں۔ .add() اور .update() عناصر جوڑتے ہیں، .discard() محفوظ طریقے سے ہٹاتا ہے جبکہ .remove() غیر موجود عنصر پر KeyError دیتا ہے۔ اجتماع (Union) | ، اشتراک (Intersection) & ، فرق - اور متوازی فرق ^ ریاضی کی کارروائیاں ہیں۔

topics.titleUr: ڈکشنری (Dictionary) کلید اور قدر (Key-Value) کے جوڑوں میں ڈیٹا رکھتی ہ…
topics.speakEn: 3.1.4 Dictionaries (Key-Value Pairs). A dictionary stores data as key–value pairs . It works like a real dictionary: you look up a word (the key ) to find its meaning (the value ). Write a dictionary with curly braces, and put a colon between each key and value. Ordered (Python 3.7+): insertion order is kept. Mutable : you can add, change and delete pairs. Keys are unique : if you repeat a key, the last value silently overwrites the earlier one. Values may repeat. Same data, four structures. Three subject marks: List [80, 70, 90] — easy to append a fourth test. Tuple (80, 70, 90) — a frozen result slip. Set {80, 70, 90} — unique scores only; two papers of 80 would become one 80. Dictionary {"math": 80, "eng": 70, "cs": 90} — you ask “What is CS?” and get 90 without remembering an index.
topics.speakUr: ڈکشنری (Dictionary) کلید اور قدر (Key-Value) کے جوڑوں میں ڈیٹا رکھتی ہے۔ کلید منفرد ہوتی ہے؛ دہرائی ہوئی کلید پر آخری قدر رہ جاتی ہے۔ d[key] غیر موجود کلید پر KeyError دیتا ہے، جبکہ d.get(key, default) محفوظ ہے۔ .keys() ، .values() اور .items() سے گھما جا سکتا ہے۔ فہرست انڈیکس سے، ڈکشنری کلید سے پہچانی جاتی ہے۔

topics.titleEn: 3.1.5 Common Built-in Functions (min, max, len, sum)
topics.titleUr: len() عناصر گنتا ہے، min() سب سے چھوٹا، max() سب سے بڑا، sum() اعداد ک…
topics.speakEn: 3.1.5 Common Built-in Functions (min, max, len, sum). Several built-in functions work across lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries. You do not call them with a dot on the object (except when a type also has its own method, such as list .sort() ). The same five functions on four structures. nums = [8, 3, 5, 3] t = (8, 3, 5, 3) s = {8, 3, 5} d = {"math": 80, "eng": 70, "cs": 90} print(len(nums), min(nums), max(nums), sum(nums), sorted(nums)) print(len(t), min(t), max(t), sum(t), sorted(t)) print(len(s), min(s), max(s), sum(s), sorted(s)) print(len(d), min(d), max(d), sum(d.values()), sorted(d)) 4 3 8 19 [3, 3, 5, 8] 4 3 8 19 [3, 3, 5, 8] 3 3 8 16 [3, 5, 8] 3 cs math 240 ['cs', 'eng', 'math'] On the dictionary, min(d) and max(d) compare keys as strings : "cs" comes first alphabetically, "math" last. sum(d) would try to add the keys "math" + "eng" + … and fail. Use sum(d.values()) — 80 + 70 + 90 = 240. The set dropped the duplicate 3, so len(s) is 3 and sum(s) is 16. sorted() versus .sort() original = [8, 3, 5] print("before sort:", original) print("sorted():", sorted(original)) print("af
topics.speakUr: len() عناصر گنتا ہے، min() سب سے چھوٹا، max() سب سے بڑا، sum() اعداد کا مجموعہ، اور sorted() نئی ترتیب شدہ فہرست دیتا ہے بغیر اصل کو بدلے ہیں۔ ڈکشنری پر min اور max کلیدوں پر چلتے ہیں؛ قدروں کا مجموعہ sum(d.values()) سے نکالیں۔ .sort() صرف فہرست کا میتھڈ ہے جو اصل فہرست بدل دیتا ہے۔

topics.titleUr: حاضری کا پروگرام طلبہ کے نام ایک فہرست میں رکھتا ہے، ہر نام کے لیے پوچ…
topics.speakEn: 3.1.6 Activity: Student Attendance System. Teachers need a quick way to mark who is in class. This program stores names in a list , asks about each student, counts how many said yes, and prints a summary with len() . Sample run. Ali yes, Sara no, Ayesha yes. .lower() means YES or Yes still counts as present. --- Attendance System --- Is Ali present? (yes/no): yes Is Sara present? (yes/no): no Is Ayesha present? (yes/no): yes --- Attendance Summary --- Total Students: 3 Students Present: 2 Students Absent: 1 Student Typed answer After .lower() present_count Ali yes yes → add 1 1 Sara no not yes 1 Ayesha yes yes → add 1 2 Absent = len(students) - present_count = 3 − 2 = 1. The counter must start at 0 before the loop. If you put present_count = 0 inside the loop, the count would reset for every student.
topics.speakUr: حاضری کا پروگرام طلبہ کے نام ایک فہرست میں رکھتا ہے، ہر نام کے لیے پوچھتا ہے، اور yes پر شمار کار (Counter) ایک بڑھاتا ہے۔ کل طلبہ len(students) سے، غیر حاضر کل − حاضر سے نکلتے ہیں۔ شمار کار لوپ سے پہلے صفر ہونا چاہیے۔

topics.titleUr: جملے کو .split() سے الفاظ کی فہرست بناتے ہیں، پھر ہر لفظ ڈکشنری میں کل…
topics.speakEn: 3.1.7 Activity: Word Frequency Counter. Count how many times each word appears in a sentence. This is a classic use of a dictionary plus .get() : the word is the key, the count is the value. Logic, step by step. sentence.split() cuts on spaces and gives ['python', 'is', 'easy', 'python', 'is', 'fun', 'python', 'is', 'powerful'] . For a new word, word_freq.get(word, 0) is 0, then you store 0 + 1 = 1. For a word already in the dictionary, .get(word, 0) returns the current count, then you add 1. {word:<10} pads the word to 10 characters so the colons line up. max(word_freq, key=word_freq.get) picks the key whose value is largest. If two words share the top count, max returns the first of those keys in insertion order. Sentence: 'python is easy python is fun python is powerful' Word Frequency Table: python : 3 is : 3 easy : 1 fun : 1 powerful : 1 Most Frequent: 'python' (3 times) After seeing word_freq python {'python': 1} is {'python': 1, 'is': 1} easy {'python': 1, 'is': 1, 'easy': 1} python (again) {'python': 2, 'is': 1, 'easy': 1} … end of sentence {'python': 3, 'is': 3, 'easy': 1, '
topics.speakUr: جملے کو .split() سے الفاظ کی فہرست بناتے ہیں، پھر ہر لفظ ڈکشنری میں کلید ہوتا ہے اور اس کی گنتی قدر۔ نئے لفظ کے لیے .get(word, 0) + 1 سے گنتی 1 سے شروع ہوتی ہے۔ max(..., key=word_freq.get) سب سے زیادہ بار آنے والا لفظ دیتا ہے۔

topics.titleUr: فنکشن (Function) ہدایات کا وہ بلاک ہے جو ایک بار لکھا جاتا ہے اور بار …
topics.speakEn: 3.2 Functions in Python. When the same instructions are written again and again, that is duplicate code . Duplicate code makes a program longer, harder to read, and painful to update (you must fix every copy). A function lets you write the instructions once and run them whenever you call the function’s name. Without a function you would copy the print-and-add lines every time you needed a sum. With a function, a new sum is one call: add(10, 20) , add(1.5, 2.5) .
topics.speakUr: فنکشن (Function) ہدایات کا وہ بلاک ہے جو ایک بار لکھا جاتا ہے اور بار بار بلایا جا سکتا ہے۔ اس سے کوڈ مختصر، ماڈیولر اور آسان اصلاح والا بنتا ہے۔ تعریف def سے شروع ہوتی ہے، نام اور پیرامیٹرز قوسین میں ہوتے ہیں، جسم انڈینٹ ہوتا ہے، اور return نتیجہ واپس بھیج سکتا ہے۔ تعریف کرنے سے فنکشن چلتا نہیں جب تک آپ اسے کال نہ کریں۔

topics.titleUr: بلٹ اِن فنکشن پائتھن میں پہلے سے موجود ہوتے ہیں، جیسے len() اور print(…
topics.speakEn: 3.2.1 Types of Functions (Built-in vs User-defined). There are two main types of functions in Python. a) Built-in functions are already defined by Python. You just call them. Examples you have already used: len() , range() , sum() , print() , input() , min() , max() , sorted() , int() , float() , type() . b) User-defined functions are functions you create with def for tasks that no built-in covers in one step — greeting a user, dividing with a zero check, writing a grade file. Side by side. Counting letters is built-in. Combining a greeting with a name is user-defined. print(len("Sindh")) def greet_student(name): print("Hello,", name) greet_student("Hassan") greet_student("Malika") 5 Hello, Hassan Hello, Malika You did not write the code inside len . You did write the code inside greet_student , then reused it for two names.
topics.speakUr: بلٹ اِن فنکشن پائتھن میں پہلے سے موجود ہوتے ہیں، جیسے len() اور print() ۔ یوزر ڈیفائنڈ فنکشن وہ ہیں جو پروگرامر def سے خود بناتا ہے تاکہ مخصوص کام بار بار کیا جا سکے۔ جو کام بلٹ اِن پہلے کر دیتے ہیں انہیں دوبارہ نہ لکھیں۔

topics.titleUr: return نتیجہ کال کرنے والے پروگرام کو واپس بھیجتا ہے تاکہ وہ متغیر میں…
topics.speakEn: 3.2.2 Functions with Return Values. A function can either print a result (show it on the screen) or return a result (send it back to the caller). A returned value can be stored in a variable, printed later, or used in a further calculation. The call is replaced by the returned value, as if you had written that value in its place. Print versus return. This is the difference examiners want. def show_sum(a, b): print(a + b) def give_sum(a, b): return a + b x = show_sum(2, 3) print("stored from show_sum:", x) y = give_sum(2, 3) print("stored from give_sum:", y) print("double it:", y * 2) 5 stored from show_sum: None stored from give_sum: 5 double it: 10 show_sum prints 5 inside the function, then returns None (the default when there is no return ). You cannot double that answer later. give_sum hands 5 back, so y * 2 is 10. Use print for messages; use return for results the rest of the program still needs.
topics.speakUr: return نتیجہ کال کرنے والے پروگرام کو واپس بھیجتا ہے تاکہ وہ متغیر میں محفوظ ہو سکے یا آگے حساب میں لگے۔ اگر return نہ ہو تو فنکشن None دیتا ہے۔ print صرف اسکرین پر دکھاتا ہے؛ اس سے حاصل شدہ قیمت دوبارہ استعمال نہیں ہوتی۔

topics.titleUr: کیلکولیٹر میں ہر عمل الگ فنکشن ہے: جمع، تفریق، ضرب، تقسیم۔ یہ ماڈیولری…
topics.speakEn: 3.2.3 Activity: Arithmetic Calculator Using Functions. Each arithmetic operation is a separate function . That is modularity: addition is one small task, division is another (with a guard against dividing by zero). The main program only asks for two numbers and calls the functions. Sample run with 12 and 4. float is used so decimals work; even whole numbers print with a decimal (12 becomes 12.0). Enter first number: 12 Enter second number: 4 Addition: 16.0 Subtraction: 8.0 Multiplication: 48.0 Division: 3.0 Check: 12 + 4 = 16, 12 − 4 = 8, 12 × 4 = 48, 12 ÷ 4 = 3. In Python 3, / always produces a float, so 3.0 not 3. Zero divisor: def divide(a, b): if b != 0: return a / b else: return "Cannot divide by zero" print(divide(10, 0)) print(divide(10, 2)) Cannot divide by zero 5.0 Without the if b != 0 test, 10 / 0 would raise ZeroDivisionError and stop the program.
topics.speakUr: کیلکولیٹر میں ہر عمل الگ فنکشن ہے: جمع، تفریق، ضرب، تقسیم۔ یہ ماڈیولریٹی ہے۔ تقسیم سے پہلے صفر کی جانچ ضروری ہے ورنہ پروگرام رک جاتا ہے۔ input() سے ملنے والی تار کو float() سے عدد بنانا لازمی ہے ورنہ جمع جوڑنے کے بجائے الفاظ جوڑ دے گی۔

topics.titleEn: 3.2.4 Scope of Local and Global Variables
topics.titleUr: دائرہ کار (Scope) بتاتا ہے کہ متغیر کہاں دکھائی دیتا ہے۔ لوکل متغیر فن…
topics.speakEn: 3.2.4 Scope of Local and Global Variables. Scope is the region of a program where a variable can be seen and used. Python has two scopes you must know for this chapter. i) Local scope. A local variable is created inside a function. It exists only while that function is running. The main program cannot read it. ii) Global scope. A global variable is created outside all functions. Any function may read it, and the main program can use it too. Local — the name is invisible outside. def calc(): secret = 50 print(secret) calc() print(secret) 50 Traceback (most recent call last): File "local_scope.py", line 5, in <module> print(secret) NameError: name 'secret' is not defined First the function prints 50. Then the main program tries print(secret) and fails: secret was born inside calc and died when calc finished. Global — readable inside and outside. x = 10 def show(): print("Inside function:", x) show() print("Outside function:", x) Inside function: 10 Outside function: 10 Assignment inside a function creates a new local with the same name. It does not change the global: x = 10 def show():
topics.speakUr: دائرہ کار (Scope) بتاتا ہے کہ متغیر کہاں دکھائی دیتا ہے۔ لوکل متغیر فنکشن کے اندر بنتا ہے اور فنکشن ختم ہوتے ہی غائب ہو جاتا ہے؛ باہر سے پڑھنے پر NameError آتا ہے۔ گلوبل متغیر تمام فنکشنز سے باہر بنتا ہے اور اندر سے پڑھا جا سکتا ہے۔ فنکشن کے اندر اسی نام کو نئی قدر دینے سے نیا لوکل بنتا ہے، گلوبل نہیں بدلتا۔

topics.titleEn: 3.3 & 3.4 File Handling and Operations (Modes r, w, a)
topics.titleUr: فائل ہینڈلنگ سے ڈیٹا ڈسک پر مستقل (Persistent) رہتا ہے، برخلاف RAM کے …
topics.speakEn:
3.3 & 3.4 File Handling and Operations (Modes r, w, a). File handling is a program’s ability to create, read, write, update and delete files on disk. Variables live in RAM and vanish when the program ends. Files live on a hard disk or SSD and stay there — they are persistent . Create a file in write mode. new_file = open('myfile.txt', 'w') new_file.write("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog!!!
") new_file.close() print("File has been created successfully.") File has been created successfully. If myfile.txt did not exist, 'w' created it. The sentence is now on disk. .close() flushes the buffer so the bytes actually reach the disk. Danger of 'w' : opening an existing file in 'w' deletes everything first. f = open('myfile.txt', 'w') f.write("FIRST
") f.close() f = open('myfile.txt', 'w') f.write("SECOND
") f.close() with open('myfile.txt', 'r') as f: print(f.read(), end="") SECOND FIRST is gone. To keep old lines and add a new one, use 'a' : f = open('notes.txt', 'w') f.write("Line 1
") f.close() f = open('notes.txt', 'a') f.write("Line 2
") f.close() with open('notes.txt',
topics.speakUr: فائل ہینڈلنگ سے ڈیٹا ڈسک پر مستقل (Persistent) رہتا ہے، برخلاف RAM کے متغیرات کے جو پروگرام بند ہوتے ہی مٹ جاتے ہیں۔ open(path, mode) سے فائل کھلتی ہے: 'r' پڑھنے کے لیے (فائل ہونی چاہیے)، 'w' لکھنے کے لیے (پرانا مواد مٹ جاتا ہے)، 'a' آخر میں جوڑنے کے لیے۔ کام کے بعد .close() ضروری ہے اگر with استعمال نہ ہو۔

topics.titleUr: with بیان ایک کانٹیکسٹ مینیجر (Context Manager) ہے جو فائل کو بلاک کے …
topics.speakEn:
3.6 The with Statement (Context Manager). It is easy to forget .close() . If the program crashes before .close() runs, the file may be incomplete or corrupted. Python’s with statement is a context manager : it opens the file, runs the indented block, and always closes the file when the block ends — even if an error occurs inside. Three ways to read the same small file. with open('sample.txt', 'w') as f: f.write("Ali 80
Sara 90
Ayesha 75
") with open('sample.txt', 'r') as f: print("=== .read() ===") print(repr(f.read())) with open('sample.txt', 'r') as f: print("=== .readlines() ===") print(f.readlines()) with open('sample.txt', 'r') as f: print("=== line by line ===") for line in f: print(line, end="") === .read() === 'Ali 80
Sara 90
Ayesha 75
' === .readlines() === ['Ali 80
', 'Sara 90
', 'Ayesha 75
'] === line by line === Ali 80 Sara 90 Ayesha 75 repr shows the hidden 
 characters. .readlines() is handy when you need a list (the grade tracker uses this). Line-by-line looping is best for large files because only one line sits in memory at a time.
topics.speakUr: with بیان ایک کانٹیکسٹ مینیجر (Context Manager) ہے جو فائل کو بلاک کے اختتام پر خود بند کر دیتا ہے، چاہے اندر غلطی ہو جائے۔ بڑی فائلیں ایک ایک سطر کے لوپ سے پڑھنا بہتر ہے بجائے پورے مواد کو .read() سے میموری میں بھرنے کے۔ print(line, end="") دگنی خالی سطر روکتا ہے۔

topics.titleUr: ایکسپشن (Exception) چلتے پروگرام کی غلطی ہے، جیسے غیر موجود فائل کھولن…
topics.speakEn: 3.8 Errors and Exceptions (Try-Except). An exception is an error raised while the program is running — for example opening a file that is not there. Without handling, Python prints a traceback and stops . A try / except block catches the error and lets you show a clear message instead of crashing. When the file exists, the except blocks are skipped. with open('ok.txt', 'w') as f: f.write("Present\n") try: with open('ok.txt', 'r') as f: content = f.read() print(content, end="") except FileNotFoundError: print("Error: The file does not exist. Please check the name.") Present Professional software does not dump a red traceback on a user. If a file is missing or a disk fails, the user should see a calm sentence such as “Please check the file name” or “Please try again later.”
topics.speakUr: ایکسپشن (Exception) چلتے پروگرام کی غلطی ہے، جیسے غیر موجود فائل کھولنا۔ try میں خطرناک کوڈ لکھیں اور except FileNotFoundError میں صاف پیغام دکھائیں تاکہ پروگرام کریش نہ ہو۔ پیشہ ورانہ سافٹ ویئر صارف کو سرخ ٹریس بیک کی بجائے سمجھ آنے والا جملہ دکھاتا ہے۔

topics.titleEn: 3.9 Mini File Handling Project: Grade Tracker
topics.titleUr: گریڈ ٹریکر پہلے 'w' سے فائل بناتا ہے، پھر 'a' سے نیا طالب علم جوڑتا ہے…
topics.speakEn:
3.9 Mini File Handling Project: Grade Tracker. This project uses 'w' to create a grades file, 'a' to add a student later, and 'r' to read every line and compute an average. It combines file handling, string methods and arithmetic. What happens in memory and on disk. 'w' creates grades.txt (or wipes an old one) with three lines. 'a' adds David: 81
 at the end. Alice, Bob and Carol stay. .readlines() returns ['Alice: 88
', 'Bob: 75
', 'Carol: 92
', 'David: 81
'] . .strip() removes the trailing 
 . .split(":") turns "Alice: 88" into ["Alice", " 88"] . int(grade) accepts the extra space: int(" 88") is 88. Total = 88 + 75 + 92 + 81 = 336. Average = 336 / 4 = 84.0. The format :.1f prints one decimal place. Grades file created. New student appended. Alice scored 88 Bob scored 75 Carol scored 92 David scored 81 Class average: 84.0 The extra space before each mark in the output comes from the space after the colon in the file ( "Alice: 88" ). int() ignores it. To tidy the printout you could use grade.strip() as well; the average would not change.
topics.speakUr: گریڈ ٹریکر پہلے 'w' سے فائل بناتا ہے، پھر 'a' سے نیا طالب علم جوڑتا ہے، پھر 'r' سے تمام سطریں پڑھ کر اوسط نکالتا ہے۔ ہر سطر کو strip اور split(":") سے نام اور نمبر میں توڑا جاتا ہے۔ اوسط = کل نمبر ÷ طلبہ کی تعداد۔ 'w' دوبارہ استعمال کرنے سے پرانے ریکارڈ مٹ جائیں گے۔

topics.speakEn: Career Opportunities. The skills in this chapter — data structures, functions and files — are the same skills used in many jobs. Python / software developer — builds applications, scripts and tools in Python, one of the most widely used languages in industry. Data analyst — uses lists and dictionaries, then file handling, to process, visualise and interpret data for decisions. Automation engineer — writes scripts that repeat file and testing tasks so humans do not have to. Game developer — uses functions, data structures and logic to build interactive games. The word-frequency dictionary is a tiny version of what a data analyst does with a much larger file of customer comments. The grade tracker is a tiny version of a school information system. The attendance list is a tiny version of an HR register. Same structures, larger files.

topics.speakEn: 4.1 Concept of Data Analysis. Data analysis is examining, organising and interpreting data so you can extract useful information. Schools study results, shops study sales, hospitals study patient records — all to make a decision, spot a trend or solve a problem. Python is popular for this work because it is readable, talks to files and databases, does statistics, and draws graphs. Five lines of Pandas often replace an hour of spreadsheet clicking. A Hyderabad college has 400 CS marks in a spreadsheet. Analysis answers: What is the average? How many failed? Is the second shift weaker than the first? The numbers are data; those answers are information.

A DataFrame is a 2-D table of rows and columns, like Excel or an SQL table. You can filter, sort and calculate whole columns without writing a for loop. Check: Ali 85+80=165, 165/2=82.5. Sara 90+88=178, 89.0. Ahmed 78+70=148, 74.0.

topics.speakEn: 4.3.3 Handling Missing Values (NaN). Missing cells are NaN (“Not a Number”). Statistics crash or lie if you ignore them. Three tools: isnull() (True where empty), fillna(value) (replace), dropna() (delete the row). Replace Marks with the mean of the known marks, and Grade with a label. Known marks 85, 78, 92 → mean = 255/3 = 85.0 . avg = df["Marks"].mean() # 85.0 df["Marks"] = df["Marks"].fillna(avg) df["Grade"] = df["Grade"].fillna("Not Assigned") print(df) Name Marks Grade 0 Ali 85.0 A 1 Sara 85.0 A 2 Ahmed 78.0 Not Assigned 3 Ayesha 92.0 A df = df.dropna() would instead delete Sara’s row and Ahmed’s row (any row that still had a NaN).

topics.speakEn: 4.6 Descriptive Statistics. Descriptive statistics squeeze a long list into a few honest numbers. Central tendency asks “what is typical?”. Spread asks “how mixed is the list?”. Marks 70, 80, 90. Mean = 240/3 = 80 . Odd list 35, 10, 15, 70, 95. Sort: 10, 15, 35, 70, 95. Median = 35 . Bottles sold 20, 25, 20, 30, 20, 25, 20. Mode = 20 (appears four times). Outlier trap: nine people earn 10, one earns 1000. Mean = 1090/10 = 109 (looks rich). Median = 10 (tells the truth).

topics.speakEn: 5.1 Machine Learning, Neural Networks and Deep Learning. Machine learning (ML) , neural networks (NN) and deep learning (DL) are important areas of artificial intelligence (AI) . AI is the broad field in which computers perform tasks that normally need human thinking, such as recognising a face, understanding speech or making a decision. These technologies help computers learn from data and make useful decisions without being explicitly programmed for every single step . You do not write a separate rule for every possible face or every Urdu accent. You show the computer many examples, and it finds the patterns itself. They are used in many modern systems: Face unlock on smartphones. Speech recognition (for example Siri, Alexa, or Urdu voice typing on a phone). Photo search categorisation (typing “car” in a gallery and seeing car photos). Medical diagnosis from X-rays and scans. Language translation (English to Urdu or Sindhi). Remember the nesting: AI is the biggest set . Inside AI sits ML . Inside ML sits DL . Every deep-learning system is a kind of machine learning, and every machi
topics.speakUr: مصنوعی ذہانت (AI) سب سے بڑا میدان ہے۔ اس کے اندر مشین لرننگ (ML) ہے، اور مشین لرننگ کے اندر ڈیپ لرننگ (DL) ہے۔ یہ ٹیکنالوجیز کمپیوٹر کو ڈیٹا سے سکھاتی ہیں تاکہ ہر قدم الگ الگ پروگرام کیے بغیر فیصلے کیے جا سکیں، جیسے چہرے سے فون کھولنا یا آواز پہچاننا۔

topics.titleUr: مشین لرننگ ماڈل وہ نظام ہے جو ڈیٹا سے سیکھ کر نتیجہ دیتا ہے — کمپیوٹر …
topics.speakEn: 5.1.1 Machine Learning (ML). A machine learning model is the system that learns from data and gives an output . Think of it as the trained brain of a computer program. In ordinary programming you write every rule yourself: if marks ≥ 40 then “Pass” . In machine learning you do not list every rule . You give the model many examples (data), it finds the patterns, and later it decides about new cases it has never seen. How it works — three steps: Worked example: a wheat-yield model for a farm near Sukkur. Step 1 — Data input. For 8 years the farm recorded: rainfall (mm), temperature, fertiliser bags used, and the actual yield (maunds per acre). Step 2 — Learning. The model studies those rows. It finds, for example, that yield rises with fertiliser up to a point, and falls when temperature is very high in April. Step 3 — Prediction. This year the farmer types in this season’s rainfall and temperature. The model has never seen this exact year before, but it predicts “about 32 maunds per acre.” The farmer plans storage and a buyer in advance. Nobody wrote a giant list of “if rain = 120 and

topics.speakEn: 5.1.2 Neural Networks (NN). A neural network is a computer model that learns patterns from data . It is directly inspired by the human brain , but it works as a mathematical computer system — not as living tissue. Your brain has billions of nerve cells ( neurons ) that pass signals to each other. A neural network copies this idea with small processing units also called neurons or nodes . These nodes are connected and pass information from one layer to another , performing calculations at each step. A typical neural network has three kinds of layer: Input layer — receives the raw data (pixels of a face, samples of a sound, marks of a student). Hidden layer(s) — the “thinking” in the middle. Nodes here combine the inputs and learn features (eye distance, nose shape, an edge in a photo). Output layer — gives the final answer (unlock / keep locked; “this is a cat”; “pass / fail”). Practical example from the source: face unlock. Step 1 — Input layer. You look at your phone. The camera captures your face as numbers (brightness of each pixel). Those numbers enter the input layer. Step 2 — H

topics.speakEn: 5.1.3 Deep Learning (DL). Deep learning is a machine-learning method in which computers use multi-layer neural networks to learn complex patterns from data. The word “deep” is used because data passes through several hidden layers before the system produces the final output. Each layer learns a different level of detail : Early layers learn simple features — edges, shapes, colours. Deeper layers combine those simple features to understand complex patterns — a whole face, or a specific car model (a Cultus versus a Corolla). A network with only one or two hidden layers is a shallow neural network. Deep learning is always “deep”: it needs huge amounts of data and processing power . Real-world example from the source: photo gallery search. A modern gallery app on a smartphone uses deep learning to recognise faces, objects or places in thousands of photos. Step 1. During training (done by the company, using millions of images) early layers learned edges and colours; deeper layers learned “wheel”, “petal”, “minaret”. Step 2. The trained network has already scanned your phone’s photos and t

topics.speakEn: 5.1.4 Components of Neural Networks. The components of a neural network can be understood through its layered architecture . Data enters , gets processed , and exits , with mathematical adjustments happening inside. Worked example: neuron calculation with numbers. A college in Larkana uses a tiny network to guess whether a student is ready for a test. One hidden neuron receives two inputs: Symbol Meaning Value x1 Hours studied yesterday (scaled 0 to 1) 0.8 x2 Attendance this month (scaled 0 to 1) 0.5 w1 Weight of hours studied 0.4 w2 Weight of attendance 0.6 b Bias 0.1 threshold Activation gate 0.5 Step 1 — weighted products. x1 × w1 = 0.8 × 0.4 = 0.32 x2 × w2 = 0.5 × 0.6 = 0.30 Step 2 — add bias to get the weighted sum s. s = 0.32 + 0.30 + 0.1 = 0.72 Step 3 — activation (threshold 0.5). Is 0.72 ≥ 0.5? Yes , so the neuron fires: y = 1 (ready for the test). Step 4 — a second student with x1 = 0.2 (almost no study) and x2 = 0.3: s = (0.2 × 0.4) + (0.3 × 0.6) + 0.1 = 0.08 + 0.18 + 0.1 = 0.36 0.36 is less than 0.5, so y = 0 (not ready). topics.speakEn: 5.1.5 Components of Deep Learning. Deep learning relies on specific advanced components to achieve its high accuracy. These components differentiate it from basic machine learning . Worked example: cotton-leaf disease detector for a farm in Mirpurkhas. Match each DL component. Large input data. Researchers collect 80,000 labelled photos: healthy leaves and leaves with whitefly damage. Many hidden layers. The network has 20 hidden layers so it can go from “green edge” to “this exact pest pattern.” Automatic feature learning. No agronomist types in “look for yellow circles.” The network finds the useful spots itself. Learning algorithm. After a wrong guess (“healthy” when it was diseased), backpropagation lowers the weights that caused the mistake. High computing power. Training runs on a GPU workstation at a university lab in Karachi; a school laptop would take weeks. Training process. They train for 30 epochs. After epoch 1 accuracy is 62%; after epoch 30 it is 94% on photos it has not trained on.

topics.speakEn: Future of AI, NN and DL in Pakistan. Machine learning, neural networks and deep learning will play a key role in Pakistan’s future. The National AI Policy 2025 highlights how artificial intelligence is now part of national planning, focusing on innovation, skill-building, ethical use and digital growth . Worked example: pick a sector and write a three-line “impact paragraph” for 5 marks. Agriculture: A cotton grower in Sanghar photographs leaves on a cheap phone. A deep-learning model trained on Pakistani crop images flags whitefly early. The farmer sprays only the affected block, saves pesticide cost, and protects yield — which matters because agriculture is a large part of Pakistan’s economy.

topics.speakEn: 5.2 Applications of Neural Networks and Deep Learning. Neural networks and deep learning are widely used in modern life. Many intelligent systems use them in the background to recognise information, make predictions and support users . Worked example: match the app to the application name — a day in Ahmed’s life in Hyderabad. 7:00 am — phone unlocks by face. → Image recognition . 7:05 am — “Ok Google, set alarm for Maghrib.” → Speech recognition . 8:00 am — Google Translate helps with an English article. → NLP . 4:00 pm — YouTube suggests a Python tutorial after he watched Chapter 5 notes. → Recommendation system . 9:00 pm — JazzCash texts “We blocked a payment that does not match your pattern.” → Fraud detection .
topics.speakUr: نیورل نیٹ ورکس اور ڈیپ لرننگ کی مشہور ایپلی کیشنز یہ ہیں: تصویر کی پہچان، آواز کی پہچان، قدرتی زبان کی پروسیسنگ (NLP)، صحت کے نظام، تجویز کرنے والے نظام، خود چلنے والی گاڑیاں، فراڈ کی نشاندہی اور معاون ٹیکنالوجیز۔ روزمرہ میں چہرے سے فون کھولنا، یوٹیوب کی تجاویز اور بینک کا مشکوک لین دین پکڑنا سب اسی خاندان سے ہیں۔

topics.titleUr: محفوظ تعاون کا مطلب ہے ڈیجیٹل ٹولز سے محفوظ، کنٹرول شدہ اور ذمہ دارانہ…
topics.speakEn: 5.3.1 Secure Collaboration (Authentication, MFA, Access Control). Digital tools allow people to share files, attend online classes, edit documents and work together from different locations . Collaboration is useful only when data is protected and communication remains safe . Secure collaboration means using digital tools to work together in a safe, controlled and responsible way. It depends on several key elements. Worked example: a Class XII Google Classroom in Sukkur. Step 1 — Authentication. Each student signs in with a school email and password. The college turns on MFA: after the password, Google sends an OTP to the student’s registered Jazz/Zong number. Step 2 — Access control. All 40 students can view the assignment sheet. Only the four group leaders can edit the shared report. Nobody except the teacher can delete the class materials. A student who left the college is removed from the class (access revoked). Step 3 — Accountability. Version history shows that Ali edited paragraph 2 at 8:14 pm and that Hina submitted the PDF at 9:02 pm. Step 4 — Privacy and safe transmission.
topics.speakUr: محفوظ تعاون کا مطلب ہے ڈیجیٹل ٹولز سے محفوظ، کنٹرول شدہ اور ذمہ دارانہ انداز میں ساتھ کام کرنا۔ تصدیق (Authentication) یہ جانچتی ہے کہ صارف کون ہے؛ رسائی کنٹرول (Access Control) یہ طے کرتا ہے کہ وہ کیا کر سکتا ہے (صرف دیکھنا، ترمیم، تبصرہ)۔ کثیر عنصری تصدیق (MFA) دو یا زیادہ مختلف ثبوت مانگتی ہے، جیسے پاس ورڈ اور او ٹی پی (OTP)۔ حساب دہی، ڈیٹا پرائیویسی اور محفوظ ترسیل بھی ضروری ہیں۔

topics.speakEn: 5.3.2 Data Protection (Encryption, Passwords, Backup, Firewall). Data protection means keeping digital information safe from unauthorised access, misuse, loss, damage or accidental deletion . Worked example A — Caesar cipher, shift = 3. Encrypt the plaintext SINDH , then decrypt the result. Write the alphabet and count three letters forward. Wrap after Z back to A. Plain S I N D H +3 V L Q G K Ciphertext = VLQGK . Decrypt: shift each letter back by 3: V → S, L → I, Q → N, G → D, K → H. You recover SINDH . Spaces and punctuation are often left unchanged. The same key (3) is used both ways, so Caesar is symmetric . Second check: CAT + 3 → C→F, A→D, T→W → FDW . def caesar(text, shift): result = "" for ch in text: if ch.isalpha(): base = ord("A") if ch.isupper() else ord("a") result += chr((ord(ch) - base + shift) % 26 + base) else: result += ch return result print(caesar("SINDH", 3)) print(caesar("VLQGK", -3)) print(caesar("CAT", 3)) VLQGK SINDH FDW Worked example B — 3-2-1 for Fatima’s Class XII project in Hyderabad. topics.titleUr: سیکیورٹی خطرہ وہ عمل یا کمزوری ہے جو نظام یا ڈیٹا کو نقصان پہنچاے۔ میل…
topics.speakEn: 5.4.1 Common Security Threats (Malware, Phishing, DoS). A security threat is any action, event or weakness that can harm a computer system or its data . Mitigation techniques are protective measures used to prevent threats or reduce their impact. This section names the common threats; later sections show how to spot them and how to reduce the damage. Worked example: classify the incident. Bilal downloads a “cracked” Photoshop. Next day his project files are unreadable and a note asks for Bitcoin. → Malware (ransomware), started by cracked software. Ayesha gets an email “Your Meezan account will close in 2 hours. Click here and send OTP.” The link is meezn-pk.tk, not the real bank. → Phishing . On e-test morning the college portal spins forever; the admin graph shows 200,000 requests from one pattern of fake traffic. → DoS . Someone opens a JazzCash wallet using Ahmed’s CNIC copy from a leaked form. → Identity theft (after data theft). The lab assistant emails the password list to the whole staff by choosing the wrong group. → Human error .
topics.speakUr: سیکیورٹی خطرہ وہ عمل یا کمزوری ہے جو نظام یا ڈیٹا کو نقصان پہنچاے۔ میلویئر نقصان دہ سافٹ ویئر ہے (وائرس، ورم، سپائی ویئر، رینسم ویئر، ٹروجن)۔ فشنگ جعلی ای میل یا ویب سائٹ سے پاس ورڈ اور او ٹی پی چھینتی ہے۔ ڈو ایس (DoS) جعلی درخواستوں کی بارش سے سائٹ کریش کر دیتا ہے۔ دیگر خطرات: غیر مجاز رسائی، ڈیٹا/شناخت کی چوری، اور انسانی غلطی۔

topics.titleUr: خطرے کی جلد پہچان نقصان سے پہلے اقدام ممکن بناتی ہے۔ سست روی، غائب فائ…
topics.speakEn: 5.4.2 Identifying Security Threats. Identifying security threats means noticing signs that data or systems may be at risk. Early identification helps you act before serious damage occurs. Worked example: read the signs in a college computer lab in Khairpur. Three PCs show pop-ups and Word files have vanished after students used a “game” USB. → Treat as malware . Disconnect from the network; run antivirus; stop USB use. Google Classroom emails: “Your account will be deleted in 30 minutes. Confirm password here.” Link spelling is go0gle. → Phishing . Do not click; report to the teacher. The e-portal that was fine at 8:00 am is unreachable at 8:05; the technician sees a sudden spike in requests. → Suspect DoS . Nadia’s Gmail security page shows a login from another country at 4 a.m. → Unauthorised access attempt. Change password; turn on MFA.
topics.speakUr: خطرے کی جلد پہچان نقصان سے پہلے اقدام ممکن بناتی ہے۔ سست روی، غائب فائلیں یا پاپ اپ میلویئر کی علامت ہیں؛ عجیب لاگ ان غیر مجاز رسائی کی؛ فوری او ٹی پی والی ای میل فشنگ کی؛ ریکارڈ کا اچانک منتقل ہونا ڈیٹا چوری کی؛ سرور پر درخواستوں کا دھماکہ ڈو ایس کی۔ کریک سافٹ ویئر، نامعلوم یو ایس بی اور غیر تصدیق شدہ ویب سائٹوں سے بچیں۔

topics.titleUr: تحفظ کی تدابیر خطرات کو روکتی یا ان کا نقصان کم کرتی ہیں: اینٹی وائرس …
topics.speakEn: 5.4.3 Apply Mitigation Techniques. Mitigation techniques are actions taken to prevent security threats or reduce their harmful effects once identified. Technology helps, but it cannot stop all threats if the user is careless. Worked example: match each threat to a mitigation — BISE e-test week at a college in Larkana. Threat seen Mitigation to apply USB games in the lab, pop-ups starting. Scan with antivirus ; block unknown USBs; enable the lab firewall . Phishing SMS about “update your portal password.” User awareness : do not click; verify on the official site typed by hand. Turn on 2FA . Fear that intercepted Wi-Fi could show passwords. Use sites with encryption (HTTPS / encrypted LMS); never send passwords in plain WhatsApp. Ransomware risk to project files. Regular 3-2-1 backups so files can be restored without paying. Shared passwords on a sticky note on the monitor. Strong unique passwords + 2FA; remove the note; awareness session.
topics.speakUr: تحفظ کی تدابیر خطرات کو روکتی یا ان کا نقصان کم کرتی ہیں: اینٹی وائرس اور فائر وال، مضبوط پاس ورڈ اور دو عنصری تصدیق (2FA)، انکرپشن، باقاعدہ بیک اپ، اور صارف کی آگاہی۔ ٹیکنالوجی تب ناکام ہو جاتی ہے جب صارف نامعلوم لنک کھولے یا پاس ورڈ بانٹے۔

topics.titleEn: 5.5 Equity and Equal Access in Digital Collaboration
topics.titleUr: مساوی رسائی (Equal Access) سب کو ایک جیسے اوزار دیتی ہے، جیسے ایک ہی ز…
topics.speakEn: 5.5 Equity and Equal Access in Digital Collaboration. Collaboration tools are vital for online learning and teamwork. To use these tools fairly, all users must participate without barriers . You must understand the difference between equal access and equity . Worked example: one class, two ideas. A teacher in Thatta starts online classes. Equal access: every student receives the same Zoom ID and password. That is fair in the sense of “same tool,” but a student with hearing loss still cannot follow the spoken lecture, and a student in a village with a weak 2G signal cannot join video. Equity: the teacher turns on captions, posts a low-size audio recording, and accepts the assignment as a Google Doc in the browser (not only through a heavy app). Now those two students can reach the same learning outcome .
topics.speakUr: مساوی رسائی (Equal Access) سب کو ایک جیسے اوزار دیتی ہے، جیسے ایک ہی زوم لاگ ان۔ انصاف (Equity) ضرورت مند کو اضافی مدد دیتی ہے تاکہ وہی نتیجہ نکل سکے، جیسے سماعت کی مشکل والے طالب علم کے لیے زندہ ذیلی عنوانات (Captions)۔ منصفانہ تعاون کے لیے دونوں چاہییں۔

topics.titleEn: 5.5.1 Functions of Equity and Equal Access
topics.titleUr: انصاف اور مساوی رسائی کے چار کام ہیں: ضرورت کے مطابق مدد (جیسے نابینا …
topics.speakEn: 5.5.1 Functions of Equity and Equal Access. Equity and equal access are not slogans. They do work in a digital classroom. The source lists four functions. Worked example: design four functions for one class WhatsApp + Classroom group in Nawabshah. Need-based support: Ali is visually impaired — share materials as selectable text (not only photos) so a screen reader can speak them; add a short audio description of each diagram. Remove barriers: post a 5 MB audio summary instead of a 200 MB video for students on expensive mobile data. Active participation: upload the Zoom recording within an hour; students whose lights went out at 7 pm watch it at 11 pm. Different learning needs: the same lesson as (a) a 12-minute video, (b) a one-page PDF, (c) an Urdu audio note. Discussion from the source: if a teacher only accepts assignments via an app that needs a high-end smartphone , is that equal access? No. It creates a hardware barrier for lower-income students. Web-based or light apps give better access.
topics.speakUr: انصاف اور مساوی رسائی کے چار کام ہیں: ضرورت کے مطابق مدد (جیسے نابینا طالب علم کے لیے آڈیو وضاحت)، رکاوٹیں ہٹانا (دور دراز علاقوں کے لیے کم ڈیٹا والی ایپس)، فعال شرکت ممکن بنانا (لوڈ شیڈنگ کے لیے ریکارڈ شدہ لیکچر)، اور مختلف اندازِ تعلم کی حمایت (ویڈیو، متن، آڈیو)۔ مہنگے فون والی ایپ پر صرف اسی طرح اسائنمنٹ لینا مساوی رسائی نہیں۔

topics.titleUr: ڈیجیٹل تعاون کے اوزار مختلف مقامات سے بات چیت، فائل شیئرنگ اور ٹیم ورک…
topics.speakEn: 5.5.2 Collaboration Tools. Digital collaboration tools are online platforms that support communication, file sharing, learning and teamwork across different locations. Worked example: choose the right tool for each job in a Hyderabad college group project. Write the report together after school, from different houses. → Google Docs (real-time edit and comments). Sunday 7 pm teacher explanation with slides. → Zoom or Teams (video + screen share). Turn on captions (equity). Collect homework, quiz and grades in one place. → Google Classroom / LMS . “Tomorrow’s test is postponed — tell everyone in the next ten minutes.” → WhatsApp class group (then repeat on Classroom so nobody is left out). Send the principal a formal complaint with a 8 MB scanned letter. → Email (written record + attachment).
topics.speakUr: ڈیجیٹل تعاون کے اوزار مختلف مقامات سے بات چیت، فائل شیئرنگ اور ٹیم ورک چلاتے ہیں: گوگل ڈاکس مشترکہ تحریر کے لیے، زوم اور مائیکروسافٹ ٹیمز میٹنگ کے لیے، گوگل کلاس روم یا ایل ایم ایس باقاعدہ پڑھائی کے لیے، واٹس ایپ فوری اطلاع کے لیے (ذمہ داری سے)، اور ای میل رسمی ریکارڈ کے لیے۔

topics.speakEn: Career Opportunities. This unit covers neural networks, deep learning, secure collaboration, data protection and digital equity. Mastery of these ideas opens high-demand careers in Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity — including in Pakistan’s banks, software houses, universities and public projects linked to the National AI Policy 2025. Worked example: match the job. “Train a model that tags Urdu news headlines.” → Machine Learning Engineer . “Watch the bank’s logs for phishing domains and turn on 2FA.” → Cybersecurity Analyst . “With written permission, try to break the college portal before criminals do.” → Ethical Hacker .

topics.titleUr: کاروباری شخص (Entrepreneur) وہ ہوتا ہے جو کسی مسئلے کو پہچانتا ہے، اس …
topics.speakEn: 6.1 Entrepreneur and Entrepreneurship. An entrepreneur is a person who identifies a problem , thinks of a solution , and tries to change that solution into a product or service . An entrepreneur does not always begin with a large company or a big office. Many begin with a small idea, limited resources, and a strong wish to solve a problem. Think of a young person in Karachi who starts by delivering home-cooked lunch boxes to a few offices, or a student in Sukkur who repairs mobile phones for neighbours. They started small. Entrepreneurs usually show three habits: They observe people and listen to their needs. They notice what annoys people again and again. They take calculated risks. A calculated risk is a risk you take after thinking about what you could lose and how to keep that loss small. It is not gambling. They improve their idea step by step. They do not expect the first attempt to be perfect. Worked example: spotting the three steps. Ayesha lives in Larkana. Her mother and other women in the street make beautiful hand-embroidered rillis , but they can only sell them to visito
topics.speakUr: کاروباری شخص (Entrepreneur) وہ ہوتا ہے جو کسی مسئلے کو پہچانتا ہے، اس کا حل سوچتا ہے اور اس حل کو کسی پراڈکٹ یا سروس میں بدلنے کی کوشش کرتا ہے۔ کاروبار شروع کرنے، آزمانے اور بہتر بنانے کے پورے عمل کو انٹرپرینیورشپ (Entrepreneurship) کہتے ہیں۔ ایسا شخص لوگوں کی بات سنتا ہے، سوچ سمجھ کر خطرہ مول لیتا ہے اور اپنے خیال کو قدم بہ قدم بہتر بناتا ہے۔

topics.titleUr: ڈیجیٹل دور میں انٹرپرینیورشپ کا مطلب ہے موبائل فون، سوشل میڈیا، ویب سا…
topics.speakEn: 6.2 Entrepreneurship in the Digital Age. Entrepreneurship in the digital age means using digital tools to start, test, improve, and grow a business idea. These tools may include mobile phones, social media, websites, online forms, digital payments, maps, videos, and simple apps . In Pakistan you already know many of them: WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Google Forms, Google Maps, and digital payments such as JazzCash, Easypaisa or Raast. Real-world relevance (from the source). Example 1: A student selling handmade cards through Instagram . She posts photos of her Eid cards, people message her, and she delivers. No website, no app. Example 2: A shopkeeper creating a WhatsApp catalogue for Ajrak . WhatsApp Business lets him list each Ajrak with a photo and price. Customers in Hyderabad or Karachi browse and order through chat. Both are digital entrepreneurship without writing a single line of code . Walk-through: how the Ajrak seller tests a new design cheaply. He photographs 3 new Ajrak designs and adds them to the catalogue (cost: almost zero). He sends the catalogue
topics.speakUr: ڈیجیٹل دور میں انٹرپرینیورشپ کا مطلب ہے موبائل فون، سوشل میڈیا، ویب سائٹ، آن لائن فارم اور ڈیجیٹل ادائیگی جیسے ٹولز کے ذریعے کاروبار شروع کرنا، آزمانا اور بڑھانا۔ ہر بار پیچیدہ ایپ بنانا ضروری نہیں؛ واٹس ایپ گروپ یا گوگل فارم بھی کافی ہو سکتا ہے۔ اگر لوگوں کو خیال پسند نہ آئے تو زیادہ پیسہ خرچ ہونے سے پہلے اسے بدلا جا سکتا ہے۔

topics.titleUr: جدول 6.1 بتاتی ہے کہ ڈیجیٹل کاروبار عام مسائل سے شروع ہو سکتا ہے، جیسے…
topics.speakEn: Local Examples of Digital Entrepreneurship (Table 6.1). Digital entrepreneurship can begin from ordinary problems . The examples below are close to the context of Sindh and Pakistan, where many students, parents, and small service providers already use mobile phones. Worked example: adding your own row. Follow the same pattern for a new local problem. Problem Digital Idea Possible First Users Students in a Mirpurkhas college lose water bottles, calculators and ID cards and never find them. Lost-and-found Google Form plus a WhatsApp group where found items are posted with a photo. Students of one college. Check: Is it a real problem? Yes, it happens every week. Is the idea simple ? Yes, a form and a group. Are the first users reachable ? Yes, they are in the same college.
topics.speakUr: جدول 6.1 بتاتی ہے کہ ڈیجیٹل کاروبار عام مسائل سے شروع ہو سکتا ہے، جیسے والدین کا کالج نوٹس نہ دیکھ پانا، کڑھائی کی دکان پر کم گاہک، ٹیسٹ کی تاریخ بھول جانا یا کینٹین پر لمبی قطار۔ کوئی خیال صرف اس لیے نہ چنیں کہ وہ جدید لگتا ہے؛ اسے حقیقی لوگوں کا حقیقی مسئلہ حل کرنا چاہیے۔

topics.titleUr: اچھا کاروباری خیال روزمرہ زندگی کے مشاہدے سے شروع ہوتا ہے۔ پوچھیں: مسئ…
topics.speakEn: 6.3 From Problem to Business Idea. A good business idea usually starts from observing daily life . Look around your home, college, market, village, or city and ask these simple questions: What problem do people face? Who faces this problem? How often does it happen? What do people currently do to solve it? Can technology help in a simple way? A short way to remember them: What? Who? How often? Current fix? Tech help? Example scenario (from the source): study material before exams. Students cannot find study material before exams. The quick answer is "students are careless", but that is not the real issue. Apply the five questions: What problem? Students cannot find notes before exams. Who? Students of a class or college. How often? Before every test and exam. Current fix? Notes are shared in many places: WhatsApp, email, photocopies, and class groups. Students search all of them. Tech help? Yes: a simple subject-wise notes organizer where all files are placed in one location (for example, one shared Google Drive folder per subject). The real problem is scattered notes , and the idea
topics.speakUr: اچھا کاروباری خیال روزمرہ زندگی کے مشاہدے سے شروع ہوتا ہے۔ پوچھیں: مسئلہ کیا ہے، کس کو ہے، کتنی بار ہوتا ہے، لوگ ابھی کیا کرتے ہیں، اور کیا ٹیکنالوجی آسان طریقے سے مدد کر سکتی ہے؟ شروع میں چھوٹا اور واضح مسئلہ چنیں، کیونکہ اسے آزمانا اور بہتر بنانا آسان ہوتا ہے۔

topics.titleUr: پروٹوٹائپ (Prototype) کسی پراڈکٹ، سروس، ویب سائٹ یا ایپ کا ابتدائی نمو…
topics.speakEn: 6.4 Prototype. A prototype is an early model of a product, service, website, or app. It shows how the idea may look or work . It is NOT the final product . It is made to test the idea and collect feedback . Think of the clay model an architect makes before building a house, or the sample kameez a tailor stitches before making 50 for a shop. The model lets people say "make this bigger" or "move that here" before real money is spent. Worked example: how a paper prototype finds a mistake early. Bilal's team in a Nawabshah college draws the three screens above on A4 paper. They hand screen 1 to a classmate and say, "Order a samosa." The classmate looks for a quantity box and cannot find one. She asks, "What if I want two?" The team notes: feature missing: quantity . They add a small "Qty: [ ]" box with a pencil in 30 seconds. If they had already coded an app, adding quantity would have meant changing the database, the screen and the order list. The prototype saved time and money .
topics.speakUr: پروٹوٹائپ (Prototype) کسی پراڈکٹ، سروس، ویب سائٹ یا ایپ کا ابتدائی نمونہ ہوتا ہے جو دکھاتا ہے کہ خیال کیسا نظر آئے گا یا کیسے کام کرے گا۔ یہ حتمی پراڈکٹ نہیں ہوتا بلکہ خیال کو آزمانے اور رائے (Feedback) لینے کے لیے بنایا جاتا ہے۔ یہ کاغذ کا خاکہ، گتے کا ماڈل، پاورپوائنٹ یا فگما (Figma) ڈیزائن بھی ہو سکتا ہے، اور اس سے غلطیاں جلد پکڑی جاتی ہیں اور وقت اور پیسہ بچتا ہے۔

topics.titleUr: فِڈیلیٹی (Fidelity) کا مطلب ہے کہ پروٹوٹائپ حتمی پراڈکٹ سے کتنا ملتا ج…
topics.speakEn: 6.5 Types of Prototypes. Prototypes are commonly divided into three types according to their level of detail, called fidelity . Fidelity means how close the prototype is to the final product. Low fidelity = far from final; high fidelity = very close to final. Worked example: one idea, three fidelities. Idea: a Homework Reminder for a college in Jacobabad. Low-fi: Sana draws three screens on paper in 15 minutes: "Today", "Add homework", "Reminder". Classmates point at the drawings to "use" them. Mid-fi: After feedback, she makes three PowerPoint slides with grey boxes and links them with hyperlinks, so tapping "Add" opens the Add slide. Now she tests whether people can move between screens easily. High-fi: Once users clearly want it, she builds a small HTML page with real colours, a working form and sample homework data. Each step costs more, so she only moves up when the previous step proves the idea is worth it.
topics.speakUr: فِڈیلیٹی (Fidelity) کا مطلب ہے کہ پروٹوٹائپ حتمی پراڈکٹ سے کتنا ملتا جلتا ہے۔ لو فِڈیلیٹی کاغذ پر بنایا گیا سستا اور جلدی بننے والا خاکہ ہے؛ مڈ فِڈیلیٹی پاورپوائنٹ، کینوا یا فگما میں بنتا ہے اور اسکرینوں کے درمیان آنا جانا (Navigation) دکھاتا ہے؛ ہائی فِڈیلیٹی بالکل اصل پراڈکٹ جیسا لگتا ہے اور اسے بنیادی خیال آزمانے کے بعد ہی بنانا چاہیے۔

topics.titleUr: پروٹوٹائپ ایک ہی بار میں نہیں بنتا؛ اسے بنایا، آزمایا، بہتر کیا اور دو…
topics.speakEn: 6.6 Prototype Development Cycle. Prototype development is not a one-time activity . A prototype is created, tested, improved, and tested again . This repeating process is called iteration . The main stages are Design, Build, Test, and Iterate . Worked example: two rounds of the cycle. A team in Thatta wants a WhatsApp catalogue for a local Ajrak shop. Round 1 Design: The problem is that customers do not know which designs and prices are available. Plan: one page per design with photo, price and an "Order" message. Build: They make a paper booklet with 6 hand-drawn "catalogue pages". Test: They show it to 5 customers. Three ask, "Is this single or double-sided Ajrak? What size?" Iterate: They add size and type to every page. Round 2 Design: Add the size and type fields, and a delivery note. Build: They make the catalogue in WhatsApp Business with real photos. Test: 5 new customers browse it. Now nobody asks about size; one says the delivery charge is unclear. Iterate: They add "Delivery in Thatta: Rs 100" to each item. Each round produces a clearer version, because each change comes f
topics.speakUr: پروٹوٹائپ ایک ہی بار میں نہیں بنتا؛ اسے بنایا، آزمایا، بہتر کیا اور دوبارہ آزمایا جاتا ہے۔ اس بار بار دہرانے کے عمل کو اِٹریشن (Iteration) کہتے ہیں۔ چار مراحل ہیں: ڈیزائن (مسئلہ سمجھ کر حل کی منصوبہ بندی)، بِلڈ (پہلا نمونہ بنانا)، ٹیسٹ (صارفین کو دکھانا) اور اِٹریٹ (رائے کی بنیاد پر بہتری)۔

topics.titleUr: اس سرگرمی میں طلبہ "کلاس بڈی" (ClassBuddy) نامی یاد دہانی نظام بناتے ہ…
topics.speakEn: 6.7 Class Activity: Create a Prototype. Business idea scenario. Students often forget homework deadlines, test dates, and required class items . A group of students wants to design a simple "Homework Helper" or "ClassBuddy" reminder system. The team will not immediately build a complete mobile app. They will first understand the problem , draw a low-fidelity prototype , test it with classmates , and improve it . This activity is the development cycle of 6.6 in action. Worked example: link the activity to the cycle. Cycle stage ClassBuddy activity step Design Step 1: interview 10 students, make design decisions (Table 6.4). Build Step 2: draw three paper screens with arrows. Test Step 3: five classmates try "add one homework task" while the observer watches silently. Iterate Steps 4 and 5: analyse feedback (Table 6.5) and redraw the home screen. Why watch silently? If the observer explains ("tap here"), the team never learns that the button is hard to find. Silence shows the real difficulty.
topics.speakUr: اس سرگرمی میں طلبہ "کلاس بڈی" (ClassBuddy) نامی یاد دہانی نظام بناتے ہیں۔ پہلے دس طلبہ سے بات کر کے مسئلہ سمجھتے ہیں، پھر کاغذ پر تین اسکرینیں بناتے ہیں، پانچ ساتھیوں سے خاموشی سے آزمواتے ہیں، رائے کا تجزیہ کرتے ہیں اور ڈیزائن بہتر کرتے ہیں۔ منفی رائے سے پروٹوٹائپ ناکام نہیں ہوتا؛ ناکامی تب ہے جب مفید رائے کو نظرانداز کیا جائے۔

topics.titleUr: ایم وی پی (Minimum Viable Product) کسی پراڈکٹ کا سب سے سادہ مگر کام کر…
topics.speakEn: 6.8 Minimum Viable Product (MVP). A Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is the simplest working version of a product. It includes only the most important features needed to test the idea with real users . Minimum: it has only the essential features. No extras. Viable: it is usable enough to actually solve the main problem. ("Viable" means able to work successfully.) An MVP is not the final product . It is also not only a drawing . It is a small working version used to test whether users actually need the solution. Example from the source: canteen app. Complete canteen app (final product) Canteen MVP Login, online payment, delivery tracking, discount offers… A simple Google Form where students select snacks before break. Step-by-step: how to cut a big idea down to an MVP. List all features you dream of: login, payment, delivery tracking, discounts. Ask of each one: "Without this, can a student still pre-order a snack?" Login? Not needed; the student can type name and class. Payment? Not needed; pay at the counter. Delivery tracking? Not needed; students collect. Discounts? Not needed. What i
topics.speakUr: ایم وی پی (Minimum Viable Product) کسی پراڈکٹ کا سب سے سادہ مگر کام کرنے والا ورژن ہے جس میں صرف ضروری خصوصیات ہوتی ہیں۔ "منیمم" کا مطلب ہے صرف ضروری چیزیں، اور "وائیبل" کا مطلب ہے کہ وہ اصل مسئلہ حل کرنے کے قابل ہو۔ یہ حتمی پراڈکٹ نہیں بلکہ یہ جانچنے کا ذریعہ ہے کہ کیا لوگ واقعی اسے استعمال کریں گے، جیسے کینٹین کے لیے ایک سادہ گوگل فارم۔

topics.titleUr: پروٹوٹائپ اور ایم وی پی آپس میں جڑے ہیں مگر ایک جیسے نہیں۔ پروٹوٹائپ خ…
topics.speakEn: 6.9 Difference between Prototype and MVP. Prototype and MVP are related, but not the same . A prototype is mainly used to show and test the design of an idea. An MVP is used to test real use and market demand . Market demand means whether enough people want the product and will use (or pay for) it. Usually a prototype comes first and an MVP comes after it: Problem → Idea → Prototype → Feedback → MVP. Worked example: classify each item. Decide whether each is a prototype or an MVP and give the reason. Hand-drawn screens of a tuition-finder app shown to 6 friends. → Prototype : it does not work; it tests design. A WhatsApp broadcast group that really sends van arrival times to parents of one route for a week. → MVP : it works and real users use it daily. Clickable PowerPoint screens of a notes organizer. → Prototype (mid-fidelity): links work, but nobody uses it for real notes. A shared Google Drive folder per subject that a class actually uses before the monthly test. → MVP : real use in daily life. Rule used: Does it work, and is it used by real users in real life? If yes → MVP. If i
topics.speakUr: پروٹوٹائپ اور ایم وی پی آپس میں جڑے ہیں مگر ایک جیسے نہیں۔ پروٹوٹائپ خیال کا ڈیزائن دکھاتا اور آزماتا ہے اور ضروری نہیں کہ کام کرے، جبکہ ایم وی پی کم از کم بنیادی طور پر کام کرتا ہے اور اصل صارفین روزمرہ زندگی میں اسے استعمال کرتے ہیں۔ پروٹوٹائپ پوچھتا ہے "کیا یہ ٹھیک لگتا ہے؟" اور ایم وی پی پوچھتا ہے "کیا لوگ واقعی اسے استعمال کریں گے؟"

topics.titleUr: ہر کاروباری خیال کچھ مفروضوں (Assumptions) پر قائم ہوتا ہے، یعنی وہ با…
topics.speakEn: 6.10 Identifying the Riskiest Assumption. Every business idea is based on assumptions . An assumption is something we believe to be true, but have not tested yet . The riskiest assumption is the belief that can make the entire business fail if it turns out to be wrong. Entrepreneurs should identify and test the riskiest assumption early , because it saves time and money . If it is wrong, you find out before building everything else. Worked example: finding the riskiest assumption. Idea: a home-tutor booking service for Grade IX–X students in Sukkur. Step 1, list assumptions: Parents want home tutors for their children. Good tutors in Sukkur are willing to join. Parents will pay a booking fee through our service instead of finding tutors through relatives. Parents will like our logo. Step 2, ask of each: "If this is wrong, does the whole business fail?" Logo (4): no, easily changed. Parents wanting tutors (1): very likely true; many already hire tutors. Tutors joining (2): important, but easy to check by phoning a few tutors. Paying a booking fee (3): if parents refuse to pay, the bus

topics.speakEn: 6.11 Developing an MVP. To develop an MVP, the team must select only the essential features . Extra features should be avoided at the beginning. A common mistake is trying to build everything at once . This makes the product difficult, costly, and slow . An MVP plan should clearly explain: the problem , target users , main feature , basic design , estimated cost , marketing method , feedback method , and improvement plan . Worked example: filling the checklist for a new idea. Idea: a college notice reminder for parents in Hyderabad (from Table 6.1). MVP Element Answer Problem Parents miss college notices (fee dates, PTMs, holidays). Target users Parents of first-year (Class XI) students of one college. Main feature Send each notice to parents' phones on the same day. Basic design Photo of notice + 2-line summary in Urdu and Sindhi + date. Cost Free: WhatsApp broadcast list from the college office phone. Marketing Students give a printed slip to parents with the number to save. Feedback After 2 weeks, a 3-question voice-note or phone survey of 20 parents. Improvement plan If parents s
topics.speakUr: ایم وی پی بناتے وقت صرف ضروری خصوصیات چنیں؛ سب کچھ ایک ساتھ بنانے سے کام مشکل، مہنگا اور سست ہو جاتا ہے۔ ایم وی پی منصوبے میں مسئلہ، پہلے صارفین، ایک بنیادی خصوصیت، سادہ ڈیزائن، کم خرچ ٹولز، تشہیر کا طریقہ، رائے لینے کا طریقہ اور بہتری کا منصوبہ واضح ہونا چاہیے۔

topics.speakEn: 6.12 Case Study: MVP for a Canteen Pre-Order System. Problem: In a college, students wait in long lines at the canteen. Sometimes snacks finish before students reach the counter. A group wants to test a canteen pre-order idea. Goal: Their aim is NOT to create a complete app immediately. Their aim is to test whether students will place orders before break and whether the canteen can manage these orders . Worked example: trace the case study through the chapter's ideas. Chapter idea Where it appears in the case study Real problem (6.3) Long queues; snacks finish before students reach the counter. Low-fidelity prototype (6.5) Paper screens: select item, enter name, collect order. Iteration (6.6) Feedback led to a short menu and payment at collection. MVP (6.8) Google Form with one of five items, used for real orders. Riskiest assumption (6.10) Students will order before break, and the canteen can manage the orders. Beachhead market (6.14) One college canteen during break. Why "close orders 20 minutes before break"? Staff need time to prepare. If orders arrive at the last minute, the pre
topics.speakUr: ایک کالج میں طلبہ کینٹین کی لمبی قطاروں میں انتظار کرتے تھے۔ ٹیم نے فوراً ایپ بنانے کے بجائے پہلے کاغذی پروٹوٹائپ بنایا، پھر تین دن کے لیے گوگل فارم کو ایم وی پی کے طور پر آزمایا جس میں پانچ اشیاء تھیں۔ طلبہ کو وقت کی بچت پسند آئی مگر عملے کو زیادہ اشیاء مشکل لگیں، اس لیے صرف پانچ اشیاء رکھی گئیں، الگ قطار بنائی گئی اور بریک سے بیس منٹ پہلے آرڈر بند کیے گئے۔

topics.titleUr: ایم وی پی کی جانچ کا مطلب ہے کہ بنیادی کام کرنے والا ورژن اصل صارفین ک…
topics.speakEn: 6.13 Testing an MVP. MVP testing means giving the basic working version to real users and studying their response . The team should collect both numbers and comments . Numbers (quantitative data) show how many users tried the MVP and how many may use it again. Comments (qualitative data) explain what users liked, disliked, or found confusing. Testing should be planned before the MVP is launched . Decide: How many users will test it. How long the test will continue. What information will be collected. Worked example: studying the results in Table 6.10. Repeat-use rate = (users who would use it again ÷ users who tried it) × 100 = (30 ÷ 40) × 100 = 75% . Did not want to use again = 40 − 30 = 10 students = (10 ÷ 40) × 100 = 25% . Comment: "Did not know order closing time" → Fix: write "Orders close 20 minutes before break" at the top of the form and in the WhatsApp message. Observation: "Forgot to enter class name" → Fix: make the Class field required in the Google Form so it cannot be submitted empty. Decide what to fix first: the closing-time problem stops people from ordering at all,
topics.speakUr: ایم وی پی کی جانچ کا مطلب ہے کہ بنیادی کام کرنے والا ورژن اصل صارفین کو دیا جائے اور ان کے ردعمل کا مطالعہ کیا جائے۔ اعداد بتاتے ہیں کتنے لوگوں نے استعمال کیا اور کتنے دوبارہ کریں گے، جبکہ تبصرے بتاتے ہیں کیا پسند آیا اور کیا الجھن تھی۔ جانچ کی منصوبہ بندی پہلے سے کریں، جوابات گنیں، بار بار آنے والے مسائل تلاش کریں اور پہلے سب سے اہم بہتری کریں۔

topics.titleUr: بیچ ہیڈ مارکیٹ (Beachhead Market) پہلے صارفین کا ایک چھوٹا اور مخصوص گ…
topics.speakEn: 6.14 Beachhead Market. A beachhead market is a small and focused group of first users . These users have a clear need and are likely to try the product early . Instead of trying to serve everyone, entrepreneurs first focus on one small group . This helps them test the MVP properly and improve it before expanding . The word comes from the army: a beachhead is the small piece of beach soldiers capture first when they land; from there they move inland. In business, your beachhead is the first small group you "win". Worked example: test a proposed beachhead against the three characteristics. Idea: an app that reminds farmers about irrigation water turns ( warabandi ). Proposed market Specific? Reachable? Strong, immediate need? Verdict All farmers in Sindh No No (millions of people, many districts) Varies Weak Farmers on one watercourse near Badin whose sons/daughters study in the team's college Yes Yes (through classmates) Yes (missing a turn damages crops) Good beachhead Expansion path: one watercourse → nearby watercourses → the whole district → other districts.
topics.speakUr: بیچ ہیڈ مارکیٹ (Beachhead Market) پہلے صارفین کا ایک چھوٹا اور مخصوص گروہ ہے جسے حل کی واضح اور فوری ضرورت ہو اور جو پراڈکٹ جلد آزمانے پر تیار ہو۔ سب کو ایک ساتھ خدمت دینے کے بجائے پہلے ایک چھوٹے گروہ پر توجہ دیں، جیسے "پاکستان کے تمام طلبہ" کے بجائے "ایک کالج کے بارہویں جماعت کے طلبہ"۔ وہاں سے سیکھ کر خیال کو بعد میں پھیلایا جا سکتا ہے۔

topics.titleUr: طلبہ گروپوں میں ایک چھوٹا، مقامی اور آسان منصوبہ مکمل کرتے ہیں جس میں …
topics.speakEn: 6.15 Complete Student Project. You will work in groups and complete one small entrepreneurship project. The project should be simple, local, and possible in the classroom . The purpose is to practise the complete journey : problem → prototype → feedback → MVP plan → risky assumption → beachhead market. Suggested project ideas: homework and test reminder system, college notice organizer, canteen pre-order system, small shop WhatsApp catalogue, college van update system, lost and found item reporting system, study notes organizer. Worked example: a completed project sheet (Lost and Found system). Item Answer Problem statement Students of our college in Mirpurkhas lose items (bottles, calculators, ID cards) and rarely get them back because there is no central place to report them. Target users Students and staff of our college. Business idea A Lost and Found WhatsApp group plus a Google Form to report lost or found items. Low-fidelity prototype Two paper screens: "Report lost item" (item, colour, place, phone of class rep) and "Found items list" with sketches. Feedback from users 6 of 8
topics.speakUr: طلبہ گروپوں میں ایک چھوٹا، مقامی اور آسان منصوبہ مکمل کرتے ہیں جس میں مسئلے سے پروٹوٹائپ، رائے، ایم وی پی منصوبہ، سب سے خطرناک مفروضہ اور بیچ ہیڈ مارکیٹ تک پورا سفر شامل ہوتا ہے۔ منصوبے کو جانچنے کے لیے رُوبرک (Rubric) استعمال ہوتا ہے جو مسئلے کی پہچان، پروٹوٹائپ، رائے و بہتری اور ایم وی پی منصوبے کو بہترین، تسلی بخش یا بہتری کی ضرورت کے درجوں میں پرکھتا ہے۔

topics.titleEn: 6.16 Ethical and Safe Use of Digital Tools
topics.titleUr: ڈیجیٹل کاروبار ذمہ داری سے کرنا چاہیے۔ رائے جمع کرتے وقت لوگوں کی رازد…
topics.speakEn: 6.16 Ethical and Safe Use of Digital Tools. Digital entrepreneurship should be responsible . When collecting user feedback, you must respect: Privacy : people's personal information belongs to them. Truthfulness : report results honestly; do not make up numbers or hide bad feedback. Fairness : treat all users equally. You should not collect unnecessary personal information or share phone numbers or photos without permission . Worked example: fix an unethical feedback form. A team's canteen feedback form asks: Full name, father's name, CNIC/B-form number, home address. → Problem: unnecessary personal data. Fix: ask only class (or nothing personal at all). "Upload your selfie." → Problem: photos are not needed and could be misused. Fix: remove. The team plans to post all respondents' phone numbers in the class group. → Problem: sharing numbers without permission. Fix: never share; keep responses private to the team. The form is in English only and has a 5 MB video at the top. → Problem: excludes users with language difficulty or weak internet. Fix: add Urdu/Sindhi instructions and remo
topics.speakUr: ڈیجیٹل کاروبار ذمہ داری سے کرنا چاہیے۔ رائے جمع کرتے وقت لوگوں کی رازداری (Privacy)، سچائی اور انصاف کا خیال رکھیں؛ غیر ضروری ذاتی معلومات نہ لیں اور اجازت کے بغیر فون نمبر یا تصاویر شیئر نہ کریں۔ اچھا حل کمزور انٹرنیٹ، محدود موبائل اور زبان کی مشکل والے لوگوں کا بھی خیال رکھتا ہے، جیسے بڑے بٹن، آسان اردو یا سندھی ہدایات اور کم ڈیٹا کا استعمال۔

topics.titleUr: اس باب کی مہارتیں اسٹارٹ اپ اور ڈیجیٹل جدت کے شعبوں میں روزگار کے دروا…
topics.speakEn: Career Opportunities. This unit covered entrepreneurship in the digital age, turning problems into business ideas, prototyping, building MVPs, and identifying beachhead markets. Mastery of these concepts opens the door to careers in startups and digital innovation . Pakistan has many incubators (for example, National Incubation Centres, NICs, in major cities) that support young founders. Worked example: match the task to the career. "Decide whether the canteen app should add payments next or a weekly menu." → Product Manager (prioritising features). "Run a WhatsApp and Instagram campaign to get the first 100 users in one college." → Digital Marketing Specialist . "Review 20 student startup pitches and pick 5 for incubation." → Venture / Incubator Analyst .
topics.speakUr: اس باب کی مہارتیں اسٹارٹ اپ اور ڈیجیٹل جدت کے شعبوں میں روزگار کے دروازے کھولتی ہیں، جیسے اسٹارٹ اپ بانی، پراڈکٹ مینیجر، بزنس اینالسٹ، اسٹارٹ اپ کنسلٹنٹ، ڈیجیٹل مارکیٹنگ ماہر اور انکیوبیٹر اینالسٹ۔ ان سب کاموں میں صارف کو سمجھنا، مفروضے آزمانا اور چھوٹے پیمانے سے شروع کرنا بنیادی ہے۔
